evidence_rules: Reading mainly develops theoretical knowledge unless paired with practice.
Observation may build familiarity and procedural understanding but does not equal independent execution.
Simulation can build execution while remaining distinct from live experience.
Supervised work provides stronger practical evidence than passive observation.
Live use adds context-specific experience and consequences.
Repeated trivial activity has diminishing developmental value.
Quality, challenge, feedback, recovery and consistency matter.
Inactivity is modeled over meaningful periods, not day-to-day punishment.
